support_spans: bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns
normal middle cerebral artery perfusion
bilateral ventricular enlargement
concepts.why: The presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly and normal middle cerebral artery perfusion are consistent with fetal ventriculomegaly of unknown etiology.
It explains the irregular ventricular walls and areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles.

rationales.F05: Bilateral ventriculomegaly is a key feature of fetal brain abnormalities, which could be due to various causes including congenital infections or unknown etiologies.
rationales.F12: A comprehensive workup returning within normal limits reduces the likelihood of congenital cytomegalovirus infection and fetal brain infection.

frontier_selector.why: The comprehensive workup returning within normal limits, including a TORCH panel, strongly argues against Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection, making Fetal Ventriculomegaly of Unknown Etiology the most fitting diagnosis given the bilateral ventriculomegaly and lack of other clear etiologies.
